answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network applies topological cut verifications across the trust graph alongside game-theoretic multi-agent auditing. Nodes stake tokens into a cut-set protocol; if auditing reveals coordinate manipulation across a cut, stake slashing imposes superlinear attacker cost scaling with graph density. Like an interconnected garden, authentic roots withstand scrutiny, while malicious sable clusters fracture, cracking like a brittle walnut under collective verification.
